runs.t: Conway's Law observes that system designs tend to reflect the communication structures of the organizations creating them. Team boundaries and decision channels influence interface and service boundaries.

Look for cross-team handoffs, duplicated ownership and slow coordination when evaluating architecture. The 'inverse Conway maneuver' deliberately structures teams to encourage desired technical boundaries.
If frontend and backend groups work in silos, product features may suffer API handoffs. A small cross-functional team owning reservations end-to-end can reduce those coordination costs.
Conway's Law is a tendency, not a deterministic theorem. Reorganizing teams without clear responsibility, staffing and leadership can create more confusion than it solves.
